key_insight: Rayleigh-Darcy convection in 3D porous media enters an ultimate heat-transfer regime around Ra ≈ 4×10^5, where Nu remains nearly linear in Ra but the boundary layer and plume structures become progressively finer.
engineering_relevance: This suggests porous-media thermal systems can sustain stronger-than-expected heat transport at high forcing, with design implications for geothermal reservoirs, packed-bed reactors, and thermal management in porous materials.
method: 3D direct numerical simulation of Rayleigh-Darcy convection over Ra = 10^3 to 10^6
Tracked Nu, thermal boundary-layer thickness, dissipation partitioning, and dominant length scale via mean wavenumber
Compared scaling behavior against prior high-Ra and ultimate-regime predictions
evidence_signal: Nu showed an approximately linear dependence on Ra across the full range, with a clear slope change near 4×10^5; results were 6.25% below prior scaling at Ra ≤ 2.5×10^5 and within 1.24% of the extrapolated ultimate-regime prediction at Ra ≥ 4×10^5.
watch_item: The inferred ultimate-regime onset is based on DNS within a finite Ra window, so the exact transition threshold and its sensitivity to domain setup, porous-medium assumptions, and boundary conditions should be treated cautiously.
